segment.description: Blackburn Fork mainstem (Cummins Fork), a tributary of the Roaring River rising near Cookeville and flowing through Jackson County past Cummins Falls State Park; catalog covers the stream, including the 14.7-mile Tennessee state scenic river reach.
segment.boundaries: TDEC scenic designation (April 4, 1968): Class I Natural River Area - 1.5 mi from the county road at Cummings Mill downstream; Class II Pastoral River Area - the following 13.2 mi downstream to the junction with the Roaring River.

coldSource.notes: TDEC scenic-river profile: 14.7 mi designated in Jackson County on April 4, 1968; 'Smallmouth bass are a favorite catch for anglers who wade the river or fish from rocky banks'; Cummins Falls (Tennessee's eighth-largest waterfall) is the river's most significant geological, scenic, and recreational feature. No dam, spring, or cold-water source is documented in sources checked. USGS lists one station on the fork: 03418180 Blackburn Fork near Dodson Branch, TN (61 sq mi drainage, no gage altitude given).

holdover.detail: No trout stocking program exists for this stream in TWRA data, so put-and-take holdover is not applicable; no wild-holdover documentation found in sources checked.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found; TDEC's profile describes the fishery as smallmouth bass, and no trout is mentioned on the TDEC page.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC's own scenic-river profile describes a smallmouth bass fishery with no trout mention, and TWRA lists no stocking program or trout regulation for Blackburn Fork.

sourcesChecked: https://reserve.tnstateparks.com (Cummins Falls guided fishing program listing surfaced in search; trout stamp 'not needed', smallmouth bass and bluegill expected - exact event URL not captured, treated as lead only)
